name: Fonab Castle
architectural_style: Scots Baronial mansion designed by Perth architect Andrew Heiton for the Sandeman family, built 1892 overlooking Loch Faskally — extended substantially in 2013 and again in 2021 to create Pitlochry's only 5-star hotel
visit_duration: Overnight stay; non-residents can book a day-spa package at the Woodland Spa, including spa-and-afternoon-tea offers
best_season: Year-round — the loch views and Woodland Spa make Fonab a destination in any season, though spring and autumn suit the walking trails around Loch Faskally best
accessibility: A largely modern hotel complex built around the historic 1892 mansion; contact the hotel directly regarding specific accessibility requirements for a stay or a spa-day booking.
tagline: A Victorian port-and-sherry dynasty's Highland mansion, rebuilt into Pitlochry's only 5-star hotel — with a Woodland Spa day visitors can book without ever booking a room
highlights: Built in 1892 for Lieutenant Colonel George Glas Sandeman, of the Sandeman family whose name is still one of the best-known in Port and Sherry production
Designed by Andrew Heiton, the same Perth architect who had earlier designed Atholl Palace in the same town — a coincidence of shared design authorship worth noting for anyone visiting both
Served as a Red Cross hospital during the First World War and later as the headquarters of the North of Scotland Hydro-Electric Board in the 1940s, before its 21st-century conversion to a hotel
Reopened as a luxury hotel in 2013 (21 rooms, 4 suites, and a Penthouse) and expanded with 16 further rooms in 2021, bringing the total to 42 — now Pitlochry's only 5-star hotel
The Woodland Spa offers day-spa packages, including a spa-day-with-afternoon-tea option, bookable by non-residents without an overnight stay
description:
Fonab Castle sits on the shore of Loch Faskally on the edge of Pitlochry, built in 1892 for Lieutenant Colonel George Glas Sandeman — a member of the Sandeman family whose port and sherry houses remain among the most recognisable names in fortified wine production. The Perth architect Andrew Heiton designed the original Scots Baronial mansion, and by a small coincidence of local architectural history, Heiton would later design Atholl Palace elsewhere in Pitlochry as well — the same town holding two substantial Heiton commissions from the same era, one now a luxury hotel and the other a grand Victorian hydropathic establishment turned hotel with its own museum.

The Sandeman family's tenure was followed by a series of institutional uses that took Fonab well away from its origins as a private country house. During the First World War the building served as a Red Cross hospital, treating wounded servicemen in a period when country houses across Britain were widely requisitioned for exactly this purpose. In the 1940s, Fonab took on an entirely different institutional role as the headquarters of the North of Scotland Hydro-Electric Board — the public body responsible for bringing electricity generation and distribution to the Scottish Highlands, a transformative infrastructure project of the postwar decades. These intervening decades of public and medical use, rather than private occupation, are part of what distinguishes Fonab's history from many of the aristocratic country houses that make up most of Scotland's castle-hotel landscape.

The modern hotel dates to a 2002 purchase by the Clark family, who spent over a decade planning and executing the property's return to private hospitality use. Fonab reopened as a luxury hotel in 2013, with 21 rooms, 4 suites, and a Penthouse suite occupying the restored historic mansion and new construction around it. A further expansion in 2021 added 16 additional rooms, bringing the property's total room count to 42 and cementing its position as Pitlochry's only 5-star hotel — a rating confirmed directly by the hotel's own classification and reflected consistently across independent hotel guides.

Fonab's most distinctive feature for visitors who aren't staying overnight is the Woodland Spa, which operates day-spa packages open to non-residents. These range from straightforward spa-day access to the property's spa and leisure facilities to combined packages such as a spa day paired with afternoon tea — giving day visitors a genuine way to experience part of the hotel without booking a room, in a similar spirit to the restaurant-based day-visitor arrangements at other Scottish castle hotels, just built around wellness facilities rather than dining rooms. The loch-side setting on Loch Faskally, with views across the water and walking access to the wider Pitlochry area, is part of what the spa packages sell alongside the treatments themselves.

Pitlochry itself is one of highland Perthshire's principal tourist towns, known for its Victorian character, its salmon ladder and dam on the River Tummel, and its position as a gateway to the wider Highland Perthshire countryside. Fonab's loch-front position places it a short walk from the town centre, making it a practical base for visitors who want both the comfort of a 5-star property and easy access to Pitlochry's shops, theatre, and walking routes.
history: Lieutenant Colonel George Glas Sandeman, of the Port- and Sherry-producing Sandeman dynasty, commissioned the original mansion in 1892 from Perth architect Andrew Heiton, choosing a site on the shore of Loch Faskally at the edge of Pitlochry. During the First World War, the house was requisitioned as a Red Cross hospital, part of the widespread wartime conversion of British country houses to medical use. In the 1940s, Fonab took on a public-sector institutional role as the headquarters of the North of Scotland Hydro-Electric Board, the body responsible for extending electricity infrastructure across the Highlands in the postwar decades. The Clark family purchased the property in 2002, undertaking a restoration and expansion that culminated in the hotel's 2013 reopening with 21 rooms, 4 suites, and a Penthouse. A further phase of expansion in 2021 added 16 additional rooms, bringing Fonab to its current 42-room capacity as Pitlochry's only 5-star hotel.

faqs.question: Can I visit Fonab Castle's spa without staying overnight?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Woodland Spa offers day-spa packages bookable by non-residents, ranging from standalone spa access to combined offers such as a spa day paired with afternoon tea. This is the practical way to experience part of the hotel and its loch-side setting without booking an overnight stay. Booking ahead is recommended, as spa-day capacity is limited.

faqs.question: Is Fonab Castle related to Atholl Palace, also in Pitlochry?
faqs.answer: Not through ownership or family history, but there is a genuine architectural connection: both buildings were designed by the same Perth-based architect, Andrew Heiton — Atholl Palace (built 1874–1878, under Andrew Heiton Jr.) and Fonab Castle (built 1892). Visitors interested in Victorian Highland architecture and staying in Pitlochry can reasonably combine the two, especially since Atholl Palace has its own on-site museum open to day visitors.

faqs.question: What did Fonab Castle become between its Sandeman-era origins and its 21st-century hotel conversion?
faqs.answer: Fonab passed through two distinct institutional phases before becoming a hotel. During the First World War it served as a Red Cross hospital, and in the 1940s it became the headquarters of the North of Scotland Hydro-Electric Board, the public authority that extended electricity generation and distribution across the Scottish Highlands in the postwar era. The Clark family's 2002 purchase and subsequent restoration returned the building to private hospitality use for the first time since the Sandeman family's original ownership.
